about: The incident timeline as data, made from timeline.md by tools/timeline.mjs (never edit by hand; edit timeline.md). See README.md.

items.label: evidence
items.text: AEMET, Spain's meteorological agency, says in public that the storm is named Charles, 2 h 57 min before the 13:17 this timeline gives for IPMA's communiqué no. 1 (row s-1109T1317). AEMET's post is timed 10:20:11 (read through Bluesky's public API). IPMA's communiqué no. 1 can no longer be read (its page and feed carry only no. 2), so whether 13:17 was its first publication or an edit is not established

items.label: hypothesis
items.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis, confidence low to medium): the official and model data are consistent with the centre passing very close to Lisbon at about 17:00 to 18:00 Wednesday, more likely just south of it (met.no's pressure minimum 986.7 hPa at 17:00 to 18:00 and a 160° wind swing in an hour; the guidance has moved). Against: IPMA's red wind unchanged, its track text already includes Lisbon, no communiqué no. 3, point models move. It does not lower the danger: the worst moves toward the passage, about 16:00 to 19:00, and a lull near the centre is not the end. Wednesday tests it: wind backing east then north and pressure near 987 hPa means it passed south

items.label: hypothesis
items.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis, re-weighed; supersedes the 00:00 reading): which side of Lisbon the centre passes is unsettled: "just south of Lisbon" drops to low confidence (was medium), because met.no's 01:19 run veers the wind through south to west with its strongest mean wind (56 to 58 km/h) at 14:00 to 15:00 and lowest pressure 987.7 hPa at 15:00, the pattern of a centre passing just north; IPMA's hourly model (an older run) and its forecasters on radio lean the other way. What holds across the inputs (medium confidence): the centre passes very close to Lisbon between about 15:00 and 18:00. The press headline "less wind for Lisbon" is not supported by these inputs. IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon stand; this is our analysis, not a forecast

items.label: fact
items.text: Checked: the "winds of 130 km/h in Madeira" in press headlines (SAPO's front page, read 06:39; Lusa, 06:37, "Charles causou ventos de 130 km/hora na Madeira") matches the figure in IPMA's warning text, and no such observation is in IPMA's open data. Lusa's article (published 06:28, read 06:37 by incident.media@) attributes it to an IPMA meteorologist speaking to Lusa and writes it as measured: "tendo sido registado rajadas que ultrapassaram os 130 quilómetros por hora nas terras altas", with no station or time; the same article also gives 130 km/h as the forecast of the orange warning to 12:00, and rain "em seis horas que ultrapassaram os 240 milímetros". So: evidence (the press reporting IPMA's spoken word) that gusts above 130 km/h were measured in Madeira's highlands; not read by us at IPMA, whose public station feed carries no gusts (corrected twice, at 06:52 and 06:53: the row first said flatly "not an observation"). IPMA's orange wind warnings for Madeira's mountain regions say "Rajadas até 130 km/h" (Tuesday 21:00 to Wednesday 00:00, and Wednesday 06:00 to 12:00); the red warning between them said 140 km/h. Observed: the highest mean wind at an IPMA station is 93.2 km/h at Areeiro (the hour labelled 02:00; the stations report no gusts); the highest measured gust is still the airport's 98 km/h at 02:30 (s-1111T0238)

items.label: evidence
items.text: the morning as one live blog has it (CNN Portugal): overnight, 66 incidents on the mainland with four floods in Greater Lisbon and the Setúbal peninsula (entry 05:44); the Porto Brandão-Trafaria-Pedrouços/Algés ferry is suspended on Wednesday while the Lisbon-South Bank ferries run in the morning (entry 00:36); nine districts under red warning from 09:00, Lisbon among the most affected (entry 06:20). No notice read at the ferry operator or at ANEPC. At the same sweep: nothing from Web Summit after its 19:09 update; IPMA unchanged for Lisbon

items.label: fact
items.text: Madeira, observed: 249.5 mm of rain in six hours at IPMA's station Areeiro, its largest six consecutive hourly values so far (was 232.1 mm at the 04:23 read); this is the measurement behind the "more than 240 mm in six hours" an IPMA meteorologist gave Lusa (s-1111T0642). Madeira airport at 07:00: wind 69 km/h gusting 89 km/h. Lisbon airport at 07:00: 9 km/h, light rain, pressure 1002 hPa and falling slowly; the south-south-east wind its forecast expects from 07:00 to 09:00 had not started. No new IPMA warning, CAP message or communiqué

Nothing on Web Summit's Day 3 from the organisers' public account or the press at this read (websummit.com is not read: on hold)

items.label: fact
items.text: IPMA lowered Lisbon's wind warning from red to orange, and starts it three hours earlier: orange wind, Wednesday 09:00 to 21:00, "Rajadas até 120 km/h" (was red, 12:00 to 21:00, with gusts that could reach 140 km/h in the most exposed places). IPMA sent the change at 07:16:30 as a CAP message (PO-01-1932) that updates its red wind message of Tuesday 07:18:40 (PO-01-1915). The red rain warning is unchanged: 09:00 to 18:00. At the same minute IPMA's own open-data feed still listed the red wind for Lisbon: its two channels disagree, as on Tuesday night when the feed followed the CAP message about two and a half hours later (s-1110T2353). Orange is IPMA's second-highest level; gusts of 120 km/h are still warned

items.label: fact
items.text: Observed at the airports at 08:00. Madeira: the wind fell from south-west 69 km/h gusting 89 km/h (07:00) to north-east 13 km/h, with pressure at 995 hPa; analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis): the storm's centre passed close to Madeira airport between about 07:30 and 08:00. Lisbon: south-south-east 20 km/h with rain, the strengthening its airport forecast expects beginning; no gust above the warned level. More than an hour after IPMA's message of 07:16:30, its open-data feed still lists Lisbon's wind as red, 12:00 to 21:00 (s-1111T0738)

items.label: fact
items.text: The whole of IPMA's 07:16:30 change, eleven messages: wind warnings lowered across the mainland. Red to orange, 09:00 to 21:00: Lisboa, Setúbal, Beja. Red to yellow, 12:00 to 21:00: Leiria, Santarém, Portalegre, Évora. Orange to yellow: Guarda, Castelo Branco, Coimbra. New: a yellow thunderstorm warning for Faro, 09:00 to 18:00. The ten messages they replace (sent Tuesday 07:18) have left the feed. Unchanged for Lisbon: red rain 09:00 to 18:00 (sent Tuesday 21:23) and the orange sea warning 12:00 to 21:00. Lisbon no longer has a red wind warning in IPMA's messages; on the mainland a red wind warning remains only for Faro (09:00 to 21:00), and red rain warnings remain in eight districts: Lisboa, Setúbal, Beja and Faro (09:00 to 18:00), Santarém, Leiria, Castelo Branco and Portalegre (12:00 to 18:00), as IPMA's open data had it when read at 08:47 by incident.ipma@; the messages were not yet in the feed at a 07:27:44 read and were at 07:37:53 (s-1111T0738)

IPMA's communiqués page still carries no. 2, with no new communiqué for the change. Also new: AEMET's table of the season's named storms now lists Charles (9 November 2026, named by IPMA)

items.text: the press on the morning ahead (CNN Portugal's live blog): intense rain may coincide with high tide and hinder drainage in the big cities (entry 08:27); civil protection counted 60 incidents by 06:00, Greater Lisbon the most affected with 26 (entry 08:26; the count for 03:30 reported earlier was 66, so the two do not cover the same period or source); an expert is quoted on the storm perhaps reaching the mainland earlier (entry 08:28). None read at a public body; the last is one expert's view, not IPMA's

No new IPMA message for Lisbon since 07:16:30. At the airport at 08:30: wind 20 km/h, no gust reported, pressure 1001 hPa

items.label: hypothesis
items.text: analysis (incident.meteorologist@, hypothesis; supersedes the reading of 02:29): IPMA's new hourly model run (07:56) now shows the same pattern as MET Norway's: wind from the east around midday, a lull of about 11 km/h at 13:00, then south 40 km/h at 14:00 and south-west 35 km/h at 15:00, turning west and north-west; MET Norway (09:19) has its strongest mean wind, 55 km/h, and its lowest pressure, 988.8 hPa, at 15:00. Reading: the centre passes close to Lisbon and just north of it between about 13:00 and 15:00 (which side: medium confidence); the strongest wind most likely between 14:00 and 16:00; the lull around 12:00 to 13:00 is not the end. IPMA's warnings are what stand: red rain to 18:00, orange wind to 21:00. Observed at Lisbon airport at 09:00: south-south-east 20 km/h with rain and mist, visibility 3 km, no gust above the warned level; IPMA's stations show 2 to 8 mm of rain an hour and rising. This is our analysis, not a forecast
